title: Energy Transfer and Motion
seo_title: Grade 8 Energy Transfer Worksheets: Work, Friction, Collisions and Conservation of Energy
standard_text: Construct, use, and present arguments to support the claim that when the kinetic energy of an object changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on energy transfer and motion (NGSS MS-PS3-5): how kinetic energy changes when energy is transferred, work = force × distance, friction, collisions and conservation of energy. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: A change in kinetic energy means energy was transferred.
key_sub: Speeding up needs energy in; slowing down sends energy out as heat and sound. The total is always conserved.
body_html:
How to think about it

When an object's kinetic energy changes, energy has been transferred to it or from it.

  • Speeding up: energy is transferred to the object (a push, a kick, a motor).
  • Slowing down: energy is transferred from the object to other objects or to the surroundings as thermal energy and sound.

A force that moves an object transfers energy: energy transferred = force × distance. Energy is never used up; the total stays the same.

Example

You push a box with 20 N for 3 m. Energy transferred?

20 × 3

Answer: 60 J

Example

A sled has 300 J of KE and stops. Where did the energy go?

Friction with the snow.

Answer: to the snow and air as thermal energy

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy is destroyed when something stops.
  • Thinking an object can speed up without an energy input.
  • Thinking a bouncing ball creates energy.

faq.q: What happens to energy when a moving object stops?
faq.a: Its kinetic energy is transferred to other objects and the surroundings, mostly as thermal energy and sound. The energy is not destroyed.

faq.q: How is energy transferred to an object?
faq.a: A force that moves the object over a distance transfers energy (work = force × distance).

faq.q: Why doesn't a bouncing ball return to the same height?
faq.a: Some energy is transferred to the floor and air as thermal energy and sound on each bounce.

items.q: Nora observes: “A bowling ball hits the pins and slows down.” Where does the energy come from or go?
c: To the pins and as sound
To the carpet as thermal energy
items.e: Energy is never used up; it moves from one place to another.

items.q: Hana observes: “A bowling ball hits the pins and slows down.” Which statement about the object's kinetic energy is correct?

Kinetic energy is transferred from the ball.
items.e: When an object speeds up, energy goes into it; when it slows down, energy leaves it.
